text: dsh-relay（DSH 插件，Web 客户端）：为 DeepSeek Harness Web 配置提供独立的远程入口，在 harness 原有回环 Web 服务前启动第二个监听器，并将通过身份验证的 HTTP 与 WebSocket 请求转发到本机。它支持浏览器密码登录、二维码或一次性口令配对设备、逐台撤销设备、TLS 证书与公钥指纹，以及可选的本地网络服务发现。适合希望从手机或其他浏览器继续使用 Web 会话的人。无需额外 API Key 或账号；首次使用需在本机设置密码并配对设备，可选择自签名或自备证书。

dsh-relay adds an authenticated listener in front of the loopback harness and proxies its web traffic for phones or other browsers. It supports password sign-in, QR pairing, per-device revocation, TLS certificates, and local service discovery. No API key or external account is required.

dsh-relay 的功能「浏览器密码登录」：在 `/relay/login` 提交密码后建立签名会话，浏览器可凭会话访问转发的 Harness 页面。
dsh-relay 的功能「二维码设备配对」：操作员从本机生成一次性口令，设备扫描二维码或输入口令完成配对并取得独立访问令牌。
dsh-relay 的功能「设备管理」：设备页列出已配对设备，操作员可以单独撤销设备，也可使所有设备和会话退出。
dsh-relay 的功能「Harness Web 转发」：通过认证后，将 Web 请求和 WebSocket 连接转发到本机回环 Harness 服务。
dsh-relay 的功能「TLS 接入」：主监听器支持自签名证书、自备证书文件或关闭 TLS，并可向客户端提供公钥指纹。
dsh-relay 的功能「插件设置」：在 DSH 插件配置页编辑监听地址、端口、超时、限速和本地发现选项，保存后应用新设置。
dsh-relay 使用前须知：默认自签名证书可能触发浏览器证书提示；可配置受信任的证书文件。

dsh-relay README · dsh-relay：[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-relay)
[](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-relay/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

Use your [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) from your phone without opening it up to everyone on your Wi-Fi.

dsh-relay is a plugin for the harness's web profile. It puts HTTPS, a password, and device pairing in front of the harness, so you can reach it from another device on your network, or from anywhere if you forward a port.
dsh-relay README · dsh-relay：It's built on DeepSeek Harness, but it isn't an official DeepSeek project.

dsh-relay README · Why this exists：The harness web app only listens on `127.0.0.1`, so only the computer running it can open it. That's deliberate. The harness is a coding agent that runs commands on your machine, and its authors refuse `dsh web --host 0.0.0.0` because it "would expose remote code execution to the network".

The common workaround is a config patch that binds the harness to `0.0.0.0` with no sign-in at all. After that, anyone on the same Wi-Fi can drive your agent and run commands on your computer.

dsh-relay README · Why this exists：dsh-relay is the safer way to do it. The harness stays on loopback, and the relay runs as a second listener next to it. Every request gets TLS and a credential check before the relay forwards it.

```
phone / browser ──TLS──▶ relay :3443 ──plain HTTP──▶ harness 127.0.0.1:3080
                          ├─ /relay/password
                          ├─ /relay/login
                          ├─ /relay/pair

dsh-relay README · Why this exists：Because the harness never leaves loopback, a relay that crashes or is misconfigured leaves the harness unreachable from the network, never open to it. The relay also refuses to start if it finds the harness already listening on a network address.

dsh-relay README · Why this exists：Harness 0.1.2 and later have a sign-in of their own (a browser session cookie). They still refuse to bind to the network, still have no TLS, and only hand out that cookie on their own page, so a phone still has no safe way in without something like this relay.

dsh-relay README · What you get：- Password sign-in from any browser. Too many wrong guesses lock that address out for a while.
- Pairing by QR code or an 8-digit code. Each paired device gets its own token, and you can revoke any device on its own. Codes are single-use, expire after five minutes, and can only be created on the machine running the harness.
- A "sign out everywhere" button that rotates the signing key and logs out every browser and device at once.
- HTTPS, with your own certificate or a self-signed one whose key apps can pin.
- mDNS advertisement on `_dsh._tcp`, so apps can find the relay without scanning your subnet.
- The full harness web UI, unchanged, with a small **Relay** link in the corner.
- A settings page at **Plugins → dsh-relay → Configure** on the machine running the harness. Changes apply when you press Save, with no restart.

dsh-relay README · Supported harness versions：| Harness | dsh-relay |
|---|---|
| 0.1.7-rc.2 through 0.2.x | **0.3** (tested on 0.2.1-rc.3, 0.2.0-rc.2, and 0.1.7-rc.2) |
| 0.1.2 through 0.1.5 | 0.2, installed from its git tag: `dsh plugin --profile web add github:sorsama/deepseek-harness-relay#v0.2.1`. The 0.2.1 package on npm shipped a stale build that can't authenticate to the harness. |
| 0.1.1 and earlier | 0.1 |

dsh-relay README · Supported harness versions：If you install a version that doesn't match your harness, the harness refuses to load it and tells you which range it needs. 0.3 depends on the settings system added in harness 0.1.7, and 0.2 hangs the web app on 0.1.7 and later, so the two can't overlap.

dsh-relay README · Quick start：New to this? [docs/GETTING_STARTED.md](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md) walks through every step with `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`, including what you'll see along the way.

1. **Remove the LAN patch if you have one.** If `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` binds the harness to `0.0.0.0`, delete that row. The relay won't start in front of a harness that's already open to the network.

2. **Install the plugin and restart the harness.**

```sh
   dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-relay
   dsh web
   ```

dsh-relay README · Quick start：The package ships prebuilt, so nothing compiles on your machine. When the harness starts, it prints the relay's address.

3. **Set a password.** On the machine running the harness, open `https://127.0.0.1:3443/relay/password`. Until a password exists, this page only works from that machine, so nobody on your network can claim the relay first.

dsh-relay README · Quick start：4. **Pair your phone.** Still on that machine, open `https://127.0.0.1:3443/relay/pair`. Scan the QR code with your phone, or open the same path on the phone and type the code. Give the device a name, and it shows up under `/relay/devices`.

No `dsh` on your PATH? Every command works as `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh ...` instead.

dsh-relay README · Quick start：You won't be asked for a password on the machine running the harness. Anyone sitting at that keyboard already has a shell, so the relay treats loopback as you. The password is for everything else on the network.

dsh-relay README · Using it with DSH Mobile：[DSH Mobile](https://github.com/sorsama/deepseek-harness-mobile) 0.8.0 and later support the relay fully. Go to **Relay → Pair a relay** in the app and scan the QR code or type the code. The app keeps a real token, uses HTTPS, and pins the relay's key, so there's nothing else to set up.

Once every app you use is on 0.8.0 and paired, turn off the compatibility bridge in your config:

```yaml
compat:
  addressGrants: false
```

<details>
<summary>Using DSH Mobile 0.5.0 to 0.7.0</summary>

dsh-relay README · Using it with DSH Mobile：These older versions came out before the relay existed, and they have two limits.

They can't connect to a self-signed HTTPS server. Up to 0.6.0 the app only spoke `http://`. 0.7.0 added `https://`, but only for certificates signed by a trusted authority, which a self-signed relay's isn't. To support them, run a plain HTTP listener next to the HTTPS one:

```sh
DSH_RELAY_PLAIN_PORT=3444 dsh web
```

dsh-relay README · Using it with DSH Mobile：That listener has no sign-in or pairing pages and can never reach the harness settings or credentials.

They also can't send any credential: no `Authorization` header, no cookies, no `Origin`. So instead, you pair from the phone's browser, the relay remembers the phone's network address, and the app is let in when it connects from that same address.

dsh-relay README · Using it with DSH Mobile：A network address isn't real authentication. It's shared behind NAT, changes with DHCP and IPv6 privacy addresses, and anything on the same Wi-Fi can spoof it. The relay limits the damage (private addresses only, a one-day expiry, removed when you revoke the device, never allowed into settings), but the real fix is updating the app.

</details>

If you're writing your own client, [docs/CLIENT_INTEGRATION.md](docs/CLIENT_INTEGRATION.md) is the protocol to follow.

dsh-relay README · Configuration：There are three places to change settings:

- The settings page at **Plugins → dsh-relay → Configure**, on the machine running the harness.
- Environment variables for a single run, such as `DSH_RELAY_PORT=8443 dsh web`. There are no `--relay-*` command-line flags, because the harness rejects any flag it doesn't know.
- A `relay` row in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` for permanent changes.
dsh-relay README · Configuration：[docs/CONFIGURATION.md](docs/CONFIGURATION.md) lists every option, plus how to set up certificates and how to reach the relay from the internet.

dsh-relay README · Before you expose it to the internet：Read the [internet section of the configuration guide](docs/CONFIGURATION.md#reaching-the-relay-from-the-internet) first. The short version:

- Forward the relay's port, never the harness's.
- Use a real certificate.
- Set `compat.addressGrants: false` and `privilegedMethods: loopback-only`.
- Don't point Tailscale Funnel, Tailscale Serve, nginx, or Caddy at `127.0.0.1:3443`. Those proxies connect from loopback, and the relay treats loopback as you, so it won't ask anyone for a password.

text: dsh-relay README · Security：Signing in to the relay gives you the same power as a shell on the host machine, because the agent runs commands there. Everything in this plugin is designed around that fact. [docs/SECURITY.md](docs/SECURITY.md) explains what the relay protects against, what it doesn't, and how to report a vulnerability.

dsh-relay README · Naming：The harness's brand guidelines ask community projects to use the `DSH` abbreviation instead of the full trademark, and not to use official brand art. That's why the npm package is `dsh-relay` and the relay's pages use this project's own logo.
